subject: Oscillating tenor consolidation + canary switch for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nebulaai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rebecca Lane <rebecca.lane@nebulaai.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — fiscal consolidation & ramp options

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, Nebula is evaluating a renewal that would: consolidate our 3 subscriptions to a single fiscal-year-aligned term, move part of the committed capacity onto a staged ramp (to match product launch timing), and optionally opt into automatic renewal with an opt-out window. We want to avoid a big upfront invoice while keeping predictable capacity as usage grows.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood co-term the three SKUs so they all align to our FY-2027 boundary?
- We need a phased ramp: 40% commit in Q1 (launch), +30% in Q2, +30% in Q3.
- Would Redwood offer an auto-renew opt-in with a 60-day opt-out notification?
- Any impact on per-token pricing or volume discounts if we extend to a 3-year commitment vs annual?

I've attached a short Renewal_Summary_Q3.pdf with our expected token profile and a SOW-draft-v2.docx showing the launch schedule. Happy to set up a short working session if helpful.

Appreciate your guidance — Samir

--
Samir Patel
Head of AI Ops, NebulaAI
samir.patel@nebulaai.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nebulaai.com>, Rebecca Lane <rebecca.lane@nebulaai.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — fiscal consolidation & ramp options

Karthik / Marissa — looping you both in. Samir from Nebula sent their high level asks (inline below). Primary asks are co-terming to Nebula's FY boundary, staged ramp across three quarters, and an auto-renew opt-in with a 60-day opt-out.

I have two objectives: keep Nebula's unit economics close to current pricing (minimize sticker shock) and preserve Redwood operational flexibility (canary switch / fallback model tiers during peak). Thoughts on: pricing delta for 3yr vs 1yr, billing cadence options (annualize vs quarterly invoicing), and whether we can include a narrow canary/fallback policy in the amendment?

If we pursue a 3-year hybrid with staged commit, I think we should:
- Offer blended effective rates with an annual true-up (protects us on usage overage).
- Allow a 60-day auto-renew opt-out but require notice tied to the consolidated term boundary.
- Define a canary switch: Redwood can route up to 8% of traffic to a cost-targeted variant during spikes with notice and SLA credit guardrails.

Can you draft two options: (A) 12-month rolling co-term with an upfront credit to smooth Q1 launch; (B) 36-month hybrid with deeper discount, staged ramp schedule, annualized billing, and a canary fallback clause. Attach proposed numbers and a short implementation checklist.

Samir / Rebecca — we'll come back with a clean amendment and numbers within 48 hours.

Best,
Irene

To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — fiscal consolidation & ramp options

Irene / Marissa — draft attached. I put together two discrete proposals as requested. Summary below; detailed pricing is in the attached proposed_amendment_redwood.xlsx.

Option A — 12-month co-term + launch credit (lower operational friction)
- Co-term all SKUs to FY-2027 boundary (co-term effective date: 2027-01-01).
- One-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of expected Q1 invoice to offset launch variance.
- Billing: quarterly invoices with annualized unit-rate reconciliation at year-end.
- Auto-renew: opt-in available with 45-day opt-out (we can make this 60 if Irene wants).
- Canary: limited to 5% traffic routing to a cost-optimized variant; rollback automated on error threshold.

Option B — 36-month hybrid (deeper discount, staged ramp)
- Term: 36 months with explicit staged commit schedule: 40% initial, +30% at month 4, +30% at month 8.
- Effective blended discount: 12% off list vs current annual pricing (net effect shown in sheet).
- Billing: annualized invoice each year with true-up; early termination clause with pro-rated refund schedule.
- Auto-renew: opt-in with 60-day opt-out before term boundary; committed minimum increases per ramp milestone.
- Canary/fallback: allow up to 8% cost-variant routing for 30-day canary windows per ramp milestone; SLA credits for anomalous regressions.

Operational notes:
- Implementation checklist included (model pinning, KV cache warmup plan, rolling canary windows).
- We should add a short audit log SLA item (Samir asked for audit logs in the last call).

Samir / Rebecca — which option is closer to your appetite? If B, I will prepare the amendment language and DocuSign packet; if A, we'll tighten credit language and confirm opt-out window.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachments: proposed_amendment_redwood.xlsx
From: Rebecca Lane <rebecca.lane@nebulaai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — fiscal consolidation & ramp options

Hi Irene / Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear options and the workbook. We reviewed both internally; Nebula prefers Option B (36-month hybrid) because it aligns best with our product roadmap and gives us predictability as usage accelerates. A few points before we sign:

1) Please include the audit log SLA item (retention 2 years, per-request export within 5 business days).
2) Confirm the canary windows will be scheduled around our ramp milestones and that rollout will include a rollback threshold (you already included SLAs — great).
3) We want the auto-renew opt-in with a 60-day opt-out — confirm that the opt-out window is from the consolidated term boundary (not calendar year).

If you can incorporate the audit log clause and send the amendment for signature (DocuSign link), we can execute quickly. Small ask: can we keep the onboarding credit applied as a credit memo rather than a cash refund?

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if needed.

Best,
Rebecca Lane
Head of Finance Operations, NebulaAI
